title: NeoPixel Mood Lamp
intro: Build a glowing lamp. Turn the knob to change the colour and press the button for light shows.

steps.title: One colour
steps.text:
A NeoPixel ring is 12 tiny lights, each with a red, a green and a blue LED inside. Mixing the three makes any colour. `ring.Color(red, green, blue)` takes three numbers from 0 to 255.

A `for` loop does the same thing for each pixel: `i` counts 0, 1, 2... up to 11.

**Your task:** change the colour to green, then Run.
hints: The three numbers are red, green, blue.
For green, only the middle number is big.
steps.success: Green! Try mixing: red + green makes yellow, red + blue makes purple.

steps.title: Knob colour
steps.text:
Now the potentiometer picks the colour. `ColorHSV(hue)` picks a colour around the rainbow, from 0 (red) through green and blue and back to red at 65535.

**Your task:** fill in the blank so turning the knob goes all the way around the rainbow.
hints: The rainbow goes from 0 up to 65535.
The blank is the top of the rainbow.

checks.label: The colour changes as I turn the knob

steps.success: A colour dial! Hue is the name for where a colour sits around the rainbow.

steps.title: Moods
steps.text: **Goal:** the button changes the lamp's mood: knob colour, then a turning rainbow, then off, then back to knob colour.
hints: Keep a `mode` variable (0, 1 or 2) and add 1 on each new press. `% 3` makes it go back to 0 after 2.
Use `if (mode == 0)`, `else if (mode == 1)` and `else` to draw each mood.
For the rainbow, give each pixel a different hue: `rainbowStart + i * 65536L / PIXELS`.
steps.success: A three-mood lamp! Changing between modes with one button is called a state machine.

outro: Your mood lamp mixes colours from red, green and blue light, like every screen does. You used **for loops** to set each pixel, **map()** for the knob, and a **button** to change modes.
stretch: Add a "breathing" mode that slowly fades the colour brighter and dimmer.
Make a mode where one pixel chases around the ring like a clock.
Use the potentiometer to set the brightness in every mode.
